Tabler 1.7 is out. It brings a nav that moves its overflow into a More menu, a number input with buttons, four new components for images and text, list group items with slots, and CSS variables for every form control. Buttons and dark mode got a round of polish too. On top of that there are more than thirty smaller changes across the framework, the demo pages and the docs.

## Nav overflow

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-nav-overflow-dark.png">
  <img alt="Nav overflow" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-nav-overflow.png">
</picture>

Keeps a nav on one line. Items that don't fit move into a More dropdown at the end and come back when there's room again. Wrap the `.nav` in a `.nav-overflow` element with `data-bs-toggle="nav-overflow"`. It watches the wrapper, not the window, so it works in a card or a sidebar too. Mark an item with `.nav-overflow-keep` to keep it out of the menu. The demo navbar uses it now.

## Number input

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-number-input-dark.png">
  <img alt="Number input" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-number-input.png">
</picture>

A number field between a decrease and an increase button, for a quantity in a cart or a number of seats. Add `data-bs-toggle="number-input"` to an input and the buttons are added for you. It keeps the value within `min` and `max`, rounds it to `step`, repeats while a button is held and works with the arrow keys. The input stays the only field the form sees, and every change fires `change.bs.numberInput`.

## Hover gallery

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-hover-gallery-dark.gif">
  <img alt="Hover gallery" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-hover-gallery.gif">
</picture>

Several images in the space of one, for product cards, portfolios and listings. The image changes as the pointer moves across `.hover-gallery`, and `.hover-gallery-indicators` show which one is on. It needs no JavaScript. On touch screens it turns into a strip you swipe.

## Image label

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-image-label-dark.png">
  <img alt="Image label" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-image-label.png">
</picture>

A short text or an icon pinned to a corner of an image, such as "New", "AI" or a video length. Put `.img-label` inside an `.img-labeled` wrapper, and move it with `.img-label-top-start`, `.img-label-top-end` or `.img-label-bottom-start`. The corners follow the text direction, so they swap in RTL.

## Mockup browser

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-mockup-browser-dark.png">
  <img alt="Mockup browser" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-mockup-browser.png">
</picture>

A frame that looks like a browser window, with the window dots and an address bar, for a page preview or a screenshot. `.mockup-browser` holds a `.mockup-browser-toolbar` and a `.mockup-browser-body`, and an image in the body fills the frame. The address bar is optional, and there's a small size.

## List group slots

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-list-group-dark.png">
  <img alt="List group slots" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-list-group.png">
</picture>

A list group item can now be a row of slots: `list-group-item-media`, `list-group-item-content` with a title and a description, `list-group-item-meta` and `list-group-item-actions`. Add `.list-group-selectable` and a checked input marks its row as active without JavaScript. Items can also be nested under a parent with `.list-group-nested`, and the list comes in `.list-group-sm` and `.list-group-lg` sizes.

## Text shimmer

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-text-shimmer-dark.png">
  <img alt="Text shimmer" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-text-shimmer.png">
</picture>

A band of light that sweeps across a label such as "Thinking…" while an agent works or a task runs. Add `.text-shimmer` to the label. It's a mask, so the text keeps its own color, and `.text-shimmer-loader` adds a small spinner in front.

## Keyboard keys

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-kbd-dark.png">
  <img alt="Keyboard keys" src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tabler/tabler/dev/.github/release-notes/1.7.0-kbd.png">
</picture>

`<kbd>` looks like a compact key cap now, and the `.kbd` class gives the same look to any element. Wrap the keys of one shortcut in `.kbd-group` to keep them on one line with an even gap. Inside a button or a tooltip a key takes the color of the text around it, and the look is set with `--tblr-kbd-*` variables.

---

## Form CSS variables

Form controls read CSS variables now. `.form-control` and `.form-select` use `--tblr-control-*`, and checks, switches, input group add-ons, floating labels and range inputs have their own `--tblr-form-check-*`, `--tblr-form-switch-*`, `--tblr-input-group-addon-*`, `--tblr-form-floating-*` and `--tblr-range-*` sets. Icon add-ons, validation icons, the OTP input and Tom Select follow them too, so one override restyles a whole form. The new Forms → CSS variables page lists every token.

The small and large selects match the inputs: `.form-select-sm` is 32px tall, like `.form-control-sm`. Input icons sit in the middle of small and large fields, and Tom Select works with `.input-icon`. The switch has a filled gray track when off.

## Buttons and dark mode

Filled `.btn-*` buttons have a thin border, inner edges and a faint gradient, and outline buttons lose their shadow. The default `.btn` stays opaque on hover. `.btn-xl` is bigger, and `.btn-sm` has more side padding.

In dark mode, nav links, list group headers, toast headers, breadcrumbs, the footer, `.input-group-text` and striped tables have better contrast. `--tblr-bg-surface-tertiary` is translucent, so card headers, footers and table stripes show on dark cards. `.card-table` rounds only the cells in the card corners.

Four neutral fill tokens, `--tblr-fill-primary` to `--tblr-fill-quaternary`, give the translucent backgrounds of badges, avatars, code, progress and range tracks and the hover state. The `.bg-fill-*` utilities use them too.

## Datagrid, Datepicker and themes

`.datagrid-horizontal` puts each label beside its value, and `.datagrid-cols-{n}` shows several pairs in a row. The Datepicker has a `weekNumbers` option, `dateFormat` patterns such as `'DD.MM.YYYY'` or `'iso'`, and a `boundInput` option that writes ISO dates to a form field. It also no longer stays stuck closed after the calendar throws an error.

`tabler-themes.css` has a new `mist` gray palette for `data-bs-theme-base`, a cool gray with a blue-green tint.

## Smaller JS

`tabler.js` is built for ES2022 instead of ES2015, which takes about 1.5 kB off `tabler.min.js` after gzip. The code is checked with ESLint now. The Sass doc comments are no longer in `tabler.css`.

## Demo and docs

The demo navbar moves the links that don't fit into a More menu. The marketing hero has a new dashboard screenshot with a dark version. Tabler Icons are at 3.49 and Tabler Illustrations at 1.18 with 11 new illustrations.

The docs have pages for every new component, a Forms → CSS variables page and an Icon design guide in the Tabler Icons section. The datagrid page has more examples.

## Upgrading

Nothing in 1.7 requires a change to your markup, and every class, custom property, Sass variable and function from 1.6 is still there.

Pricing and Shape moved from `tabler-marketing.css` into the core `tabler.css`. A page that loads both files needs no change. A page that loaded only `tabler-marketing.css` for `.pricing` or `.shape` has to add `tabler.css`. If you import Sass partials one by one, `scss/marketing/pricing` and `scss/marketing/shape` are now `scss/ui/pricing` and `scss/ui/shape`.

Some things look a little different: buttons, the switch track, the small select height and a few dark mode surfaces. Check custom styles that sit close to them.

Every change, with a before and after example, is in the [Upgrade to 1.7](https://docs.tabler.io/ui/getting-started/upgrade/1-7) guide.
